A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UnKE method and UnKEBench benchmark. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original automatic and human evaluations, structured knowledge editing experiments, ablations, and batch and sequential editing results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons, locality measurements, and UnKE results on KnowEdit.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same non-local block key-value representation, last-token optimization, and three-loss objective. Equations 1–7 and UnKE's two-stage editing procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds actual KnowEdit evaluation on WikiData_recent, ZsRE, WikiBio, WikiData_counterfact, ConvSent, and Sanitation (Appendix F, Table 8), substantially extending evaluated coverage. UnKEBench also gains unrelated knowledge questions constructed from Wikipedia triples for locality evaluation. Its original 1,000 counterfactual texts and the earlier evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds LoRA, AdaLoRA, RECT, and IKE with and without ICL to the retained FT-A, FT-L, ROME, MEMIT, and MEND comparisons. The new KnowEdit comparison additionally includes SERAC, ICE, and FT-M as labeled in Table 8. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 adds Loc-FactScore evaluation on unrelated questions and KnowEdit evaluations reporting editing success, portability, locality, and fluency. New baseline protocols include IKE answer-containing prompts with or without five retrieved examples and LoRA/AdaLoRA tuning. The retained UnKEBench batch size, decoding temperature, editing layer, and human-evaluation design are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a direct assessment of unrelated-fact preservation through Loc-FactScore and qualitative LoRA/AdaLoRA convergence and hyperparameter-sensitivity observations in Appendix J. The original module/loss ablations, layer sweep, batch and sequential editing analyses, human-correlation analysis, and generation case study remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three-annotator evaluation of 36 samples per method, Fleiss' kappa of 0.57, and Pearson correlations with p-values. v3 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or other uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: v3 adds baseline, locality, and KnowEdit results. IKE obtains FactScores of 94.60 without ICL and 93.08 with ICL, exceeding UnKE's retained 42.49. Existing metric assignments also change: Table 4's UnKE Bert-Score changes from 98.63/76.85 to 99.61/93.09. The layer-7 MMLU entry changes from 29.72 to 29.68, and reported FT-L/FT-A runtimes change from 24/31 to 14/21 hours. These are added or revised reported results, not demonstrated improvements to UnKE itself.

T1.justification: The knowledge-localization hypotheses, mathematical representation, and optimization derivations are retained. Equations 1–7 are unchanged, and v3 introduces no new theorem, proof, or substantive formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: UnKEBench, non-local block key-value storage, cause-driven optimization, and effectiveness on structured and unstructured editing with batch and sequential capabilities. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 materially revises the comparative interpretation. Where v2 emphasizes UnKE's leading FactScore and little general-capability impact, v3 acknowledges IKE's much higher FactScore, attributes it to reading comprehension with supplied answers, and characterizes this as 'cheating'. It also introduces a locality tradeoff attributed to UnKE modifying more parameters. Appendix F qualifies KnowEdit advantages by dataset.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly documents benchmark checks, including matching thresholds of 0.8 and 0.9, entity consistency, regeneration rules, and a 15-token sub-answer limit. Appendix J adds LoRA/AdaLoRA settings, RECT tuning information, and IKE templates, retrieval, and inference details. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation; they do not establish that the previously used benchmark was regenerated. UnKE's own settings and code link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds AKEW and LEME and distinguishes their entity-concept editing from UnKEBench's direct unstructured-text editing. Additional references address parameter memory and downstream applications. These are localized additions; the existing related-work taxonomy and principal research positioning remain.

P1.justification: Most core prose remains unchanged. Benchmark construction moves from Section 5.1 to Appendix A, Section 5.1 becomes Evaluation Metrics, and the experimental discussion and appendix documentation expand. There are localized wording, cross-reference, author-header, and acknowledgement edits rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The principal comparison in Table 2 is substantially expanded with baseline rows and a locality column, while v3 adds the extensive KnowEdit table and two IKE prompt tables. Figure 1 moves earlier and its caption is shortened; appendix tables and prompt examples are relocated or reformatted. The original four figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens weaknesses in v2's empirical support: Table 2 introduces competitive parameter-efficient and in-context baselines and directly tests unrelated-knowledge retention, exposing meaningful tradeoffs. KnowEdit broadens the test of applicability, while benchmark-validation and implementation details improve reproducibility. Corrected metric assignments also improve consistency across tables. The dismissive treatment of IKE's advantage and the unfinished RECT configuration sentence are weaknesses, but the gains in evidential coverage and transparency clearly outweigh them.
